title: Question of Esperet and Raymond on improvability of expansion bounds
statement_text: Can either of the bounds $\max\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1,\,0\right)\leq b_\varepsilon\leq\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon}-1$ and $B_\varepsilon\leq\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon}-1$ be improved (in particular, in terms of the multiplicative constants in the exponents)?
context_text: Corollary 2 (derived from Plotkin–Rao–Smith) and Theorem 5 (Esperet–Raymond) together yield the bounds on $b_\varepsilon$ and $B_\varepsilon$, the extreme exponents governing the expansion of hereditary graph classes whose balanced-separator function satisfies $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\Theta(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. Esperet and Raymond asked whether either bound could be substantially improved, suggesting that $d$-dimensional grids might provide insight.
paper_contribution: Shows that neither exponent can be substantially improved: $B_\varepsilon=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}-1$ exactly (matching the upper bound), $b_\varepsilon=0$ for $\frac{1}{2}\leq\varepsilon\leq 1$, and $b_\varepsilon\leq\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}-\frac{1}{2}$ for $0<\varepsilon<\frac{1}{2}$, leaving a gap of at most $\frac{1}{2}$ above the lower bound $\frac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1$.
notes: The original question is not stated in a formal labelled environment in this paper; reconstructed from prose. PDF source.
paper_title: A note on sublinear separators and expansion

title: Informal open question on the exact value of $b_\varepsilon$
statement_text: It is unclear whether the upper or the lower bound on $b_\varepsilon$ can be improved for $0<\varepsilon<\frac{1}{2}$. While the fact that $b_{1/2}=0$ matches the lower bound suggests that a better construction improving the upper bound in general could exist, it is also plausible that this is just a "dimension 2" artifact and in fact the lower bound might be possible to improve for $\varepsilon<1/2$ (possibly leading to discontinuity of $b_\varepsilon$ at $\varepsilon=1/2$).
context_text:
For an $n$-vertex graph, a balanced separator is a set $X$ of vertices such that each component of $G-X$ has at most $2n/3$ vertices; $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a balanced separator, and for a class $\mathcal{G}$, $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\max\{s(G):G\in\mathcal{G},|V(G)|\le n\}$. An $r$-shallow minor of $G$ is a graph obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint subgraphs of radius at most $r$; $
abla_r(G)$ is the maximum density $|E(H)|/|V(H)|$ of an $r$-shallow minor $H$ of $G$, and $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=\sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}}
abla_r(G)$ (the expansion of $\mathcal{G}$). For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $b_\varepsilon$ is the supremum of reals $b$ such that every hereditary class $\mathcal{G}$ with $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\Theta(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ satisfies $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=\Omega(r^b)$, and $B_\varepsilon$ is the infimum of reals $B$ such that every such class satisfies $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=O(r^B)$. Results of Plotkin, Rao and Smith and of Esperet and Raymond give $\max( rac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1,0)\le b_\varepsilon\le B_\varepsilon\le rac1\varepsilon-1$, and Esperet and Raymond asked whether these bounds can be improved. The author shows that $B_\varepsilon= rac1\varepsilon-1$ for all $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $b_\varepsilon=0$ for $ rac12\le\varepsilon\le1$, and $ rac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1\le b_\varepsilon\le rac{1}{2\varepsilon}- rac12$ for $0<\varepsilon< rac12$, so the bounds on $b_\varepsilon$ differ by at most $ rac12$. The value $b_{1/2}=0$ is witnessed by planar graphs, which have separators of order $\Theta(n^{1/2})$ (Lipton and Tarjan) and all of whose minors have density at most $3$.
notes: Stated as an open remark in the concluding summary. PDF source.

title: Informal conjecture $b'_\varepsilon = b_\varepsilon$ for $0<\varepsilon<\tfrac{1}{2}$
statement_text: It seems likely that $b'_\varepsilon = b_\varepsilon$ when $0 < \varepsilon < \frac{1}{2}$ as well.
context_text:
For an $n$-vertex graph, a balanced separator is a set $X$ of vertices such that each component of $G-X$ has at most $2n/3$ vertices; $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a balanced separator, and for a class $\mathcal{G}$, $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\max\{s(G):G\in\mathcal{G},|V(G)|\le n\}$. An $r$-shallow minor of $G$ is a graph obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint subgraphs of radius at most $r$; $
abla_r(G)$ is the maximum density $|E(H)|/|V(H)|$ of an $r$-shallow minor $H$ of $G$, and $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=\sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}}
abla_r(G)$ (the expansion of $\mathcal{G}$). For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $b_\varepsilon$ is the supremum of reals $b$ such that every hereditary class $\mathcal{G}$ with $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\Theta(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ satisfies $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=\Omega(r^b)$, and $B_\varepsilon$ is the infimum of reals $B$ such that every such class satisfies $
abla_\mathcal{G}(r)=O(r^B)$. The variants $b'_\varepsilon$ and $B'_\varepsilon$ are defined in the same way, except that $b'_\varepsilon$ only requires $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ and $B'_\varepsilon$ only requires $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. The author proves $\max( rac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1,0)\le b'_\varepsilon\le b_\varepsilon\le B_\varepsilon\le B'_\varepsilon\le rac1\varepsilon-1$, hence $b'_\varepsilon=b_\varepsilon=0$ for $ rac12\le\varepsilon\le1$, $B'_\varepsilon=B_\varepsilon= rac1\varepsilon-1$ for all $\varepsilon$, and $ rac{1}{2\varepsilon}-1\le b'_\varepsilon\le b_\varepsilon\le rac{1}{2\varepsilon}- rac12$ for $0<\varepsilon< rac12$. Equality $b'_\varepsilon=b_\varepsilon$ is not obvious: from a class $\mathcal{G}'$ with $s_{\mathcal{G}'}(n)=\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ (which may be assumed closed under subgraphs), the natural hereditary class $\mathcal{G}$ of its graphs all of whose induced subgraphs $H$ satisfy $s(H)=O(|V(H)|^{1-\varepsilon})$ need not satisfy $s_\mathcal{G}(n)=\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$.
notes: Conjectural language 'It seems likely' appears in the final section. PDF source.
